title: RIT Dorm Laundry Tracker
tagline: My first team prototype for checking dorm washers and dryers before walking downstairs
summary: This was one of my first team software projects at RIT. We made a prototype where students could pick their dorm, see which washers and dryers were free, and start a 55-minute laundry timer. It's also where I met my friend Jimmy, who I'm still friends with today.

overview.what: A prototype website where RIT students pick their dorm, see which washers and dryers are free, and start a 55-minute laundry timer.
overview.why: It was our team project for SWEN 101: check if a machine is free before you walk downstairs.
overview.did: I worked with my team to plan the app, split up the pages, share our code and put it all together, in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
overview.result: It was only a front end, not connected to real machines, but it was my first real team project, and it's where I met my friend Jimmy.

hero.alt: RIT dorm laundry page showing Kate Gleason Hall washers outlined in green when available and red when in use
hero.caption: Which washers and dryers are free.

sections.heading: My first team experience
body: The most important part of this project for me was learning how to work on software with a team for the first time. We had to agree on what the app should do, divide up the pages and features, share our code, and bring it all back together into one flow.
It was a great intro to working with people instead of building everything alone. I also met my friend Jimmy through this project, and we're still friends today.

sections.heading: Choosing a dorm
body: It starts with a simple RIT email login and then asks you to pick one of thirteen residence halls. The dorm you pick is saved in localStorage and carried over to the machine page.

media.alt: Dorm selection page listing RIT residence halls over a campus photograph
media.caption: Pick your residence hall first.

sections.heading: Availability and timers
body: Free washers and dryers have a green outline, and machines in use have a red one. Picking a free machine opens a status page with a 55-minute countdown.

It was only a front end, not hooked up to anything on campus. We designed a JSON layout for thirteen dorms with eight machines each, but the final pages still had the machine states hardcoded, and the timer reset if you refreshed the page.

media.alt: Orange washer status page showing a 55-minute countdown and a button to start the timer
media.caption: The washer countdown, before it starts.

notes: DRAFT CREATED FROM USER INTERVIEW AND A LOCAL RUN. The app was served from SWENGroup-1/ and the complete flow was verified: login, dorm selection, machine availability, and washer timer. The three screenshots were captured from that run on 2026-09-13. GitHub API confirmed Michael-Lizzio/SWENGroup-1 is public but GitHub Pages is not enabled, so only the repository is linked and no live-demo claim is made. Date 2024-10 comes from the data generator's authored date; the repository was pushed in December 2024. The visible copy intentionally says this is a front-end prototype because machine_data.json is never loaded and availability remains hardcoded. User supplied the personal context about meeting Jimmy and remaining friends.
